findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (missing file, permissions, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or absent filesystem input causes thread panic instead of returning a typed parse/I/O error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, IOError> and propagate with ? or match; never unwrap fs I/O

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric input (overflow, bad digits, empty string)
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV data aborts the entire session load instead of yielding a per-record parse error
findings.fix: Use parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ParseError::BadValue { ... }) and propagate; return Result<Vec<Record>, RecordError>

findings.problem: as u16 lossy cast truncates u32 values > 65535 silently
findings.failure_mode: values in 65536..u32::MAX are silently truncated to u16 range, producing incorrect records with no error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(val).map_err(...) to produce a typed overflow error, or parse directly as u16

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() then parts[0]/parts[1] indexing allocates a Vec and uses unchecked indexing
findings.failure_mode: allocates a Vec<String> per line unnecessarily; parts[0] and parts[1] may panic with IndexOutOfBounds if the line has fewer than 2 comma-separated fields
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').map_err(...) for first-delimiter extraction; handle missing second field with a typed error; avoid collect()

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is hidden I/O side effect inside a parsing function
findings.failure_mode: breaks purity of the parsing logic, makes the function untestable in isolation, and produces stdout noise in benchmarks and tests
findings.fix: Remove println!; if logging is needed, push it to the imperative shell layer (caller) or use a logger abstraction injected as a parameter

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> with no Result type; all fallible operations (I/O, parse, cast) are hidden behind unwrap
findings.failure_mode: caller has no way to distinguish missing file, malformed line, or overflow; error context is lost at panic
findings.fix: Signature should be fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> with a domain-typed error enum

findings.problem: load_sessions performs fs::read_to_string directly — I/O mixed into what should be a parse-only concern
findings.failure_mode: cannot unit-test parsing logic without filesystem setup; violates functional core / imperative shell split
findings.fix: Split into shell fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> that reads the file, and pure fn parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> that handles all parsing
